claim: For required structural gap q under maximum query arity b>=2, higher arity can reduce minimum adaptive/query/frontier burden but cannot reduce the minimum represented-world count; the exact joint requirement is therefore generally a Pareto frontier.

q2_b3.interpretation: world and query/frontier minima are simultaneously attainable

q3_b4.interpretation: query/frontier optimum and world optimum are incompatible; neither point dominates the other

q8_b3.interpretation: higher arity again produces a genuine world-query tradeoff

registered_audits.world_minimum_arity_invariance: q=1..40 checked against exact unrestricted world-gap ceiling n-1-ceil(log2 n)
registered_audits.log_b_depth_bracket: b=2..7 and q=1..500 checked for h_b*(q) in {ceil(log_b((b-1)q+1)), that value + 1}
registered_audits.constructive_exact_solver: all Pareto points in q=3,b=4 and q=2,b=3 examples are converted to private-pair tasks and checked for exact C_A, C_F, and productive-frontier edge count
registered_audits.pareto_recurrence: points use the inherited exact F_b(n,h) recurrence; only strict decreases in minimum world count are retained as query count rises with depth

novelty_boundary: No novelty claim for elementary b-ary tree counting. The repository-specific contribution is the composition with adaptive/fixed structural gap and productive-frontier obligations, yielding a dynamical-reachability Pareto constraint.
